_comment: The core sleeve's opportunity set. One line per exposure, not per fund:
six ETFs tracking 沪深300 are one exposure, and risk parity over duplicates
just splits a position into six tickets.
`role` is what the allocator reads. `exposure` is documentation for a human
and a key for the correlation check (two names in the same bucket are not
This file is the single source of truth: configs/data.json's etf_codes must
contain every code here (a test enforces it), and core.py reads `role`.
It used to be two hardcoded tuples that had already drifted: 512690 was
downloaded for two years and never allocated a cent.

defensive.name: 国债5年
defensive._note: A 100-share lot costs about CNY 14,700, so a CNY 5,000 book cannot hold it and the defensive sleeve stays in cash. That is an account-size limit, not a choice.

_max_positions_note: Measured, not guessed. Over 22 trend-on quarterly samples 2018-2026 on a
3 positions -> 72% invested, 3.0 held, 0.0 names per rebalance unbuyable
Each extra name buys about half a holding and costs 5-7 points of exposure,
because a 1/6 share of 5,000 is 830 CNY and one lot of 510300 already costs
582. Four is where that curve bends. It is a property of the account size,
not of the strategy: at a larger account this number should rise.
_retired_note: Retired 2026-11-01 by the account owner, not by the model. Undo by setting
this to false; nothing else has to change.
Why: the rule's defensive leg is 511010 at ~141 a share, so one lot is
14,112 against a 5,007 book - 2.8x. Every defensive day therefore produced a
100% cash row and a flat 0.00% return, which reads on the arena page as a
strategy holding cash on purpose. It was not: the instrument it asks for
cannot be bought at this size. Six sessions of that is six rows of noise,
and no size of position makes the sleeve expressible while equity < 14,112.
What retirement does: /core/plan and /core/execute return 409 CORE_RETIRED,
the daily job stops writing core_nav rows, and the arena stops listing the
sleeve. What it does NOT do: delete the six existing rows (they are the
audit trail of the decision), or stop /core from reporting the numbers -
`state`, `executable` and `required_nav` stay readable so the reason is
Re-enable only with a defensive instrument whose lot fits the book, or with
equity above the required_nav that /core reports.
